annotationRationale: Strict ordering fixes the arrangement of each chosen digit set. Direct subset counting and reversal pairing give distinct ways to handle the special role of zero.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independent counting gives U=502 and D=1013, hence an absolute difference of 511, choice E. The digit restrictions and recorded key are consistent; no figure is needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful supplied approaches are retained: reversal cancellation and separate subset counts. Binomial-coefficient sums would restate the subset counting and are unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Unordered digit selection supports the assessed combinations-application node, and binary inclusion choices support the multiplication-principle node. The reversal method additionally carries the precise bijective-counting node.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Reversal gives an invertible pairing between all upnos and exactly the zero-free downnos. Every remaining downno ends in zero and corresponds uniquely to a nonempty subset of the nine nonzero digits. Their count is 2^9-1=511, including the ten-digit case and excluding zero alone.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 3 and 7 support the reversal and unmatched-subset approach. The candidate supplies original explanatory prose and explicit inverse checks; source-informed-original is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation establishes why zero distinguishes the families, verifies the pairing in both directions, and explains both the power-of-two count and the excluded empty choice. No unfamiliar prerequisite is left unexplained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Bijective-counting exactly matches reversal and subset reconstruction. cnm_h231 matches the nine independent include-or-exclude decisions.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Upnos correspond to subsets of nine nonzero digits of size at least two, giving 512-1-9=502. Downnos correspond to subsets of all ten digits of size at least two, giving 1024-1-10=1013. Such a downno necessarily starts with a nonzero digit. The difference is 511.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solutions 1 and 6 supply the separate subset counts. The candidate explains the correspondences independently and correctly uses source-informed-original rather than claiming official MAA authorship.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation makes fixed ordering, absence of repeated digits, leading-zero validity, and both exclusions explicit. Binary decisions justify the subset totals without requiring a binomial identity.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h239 fits recognizing unordered selection rather than freely arranging digits; cnm_h231 fits computing all subsets through binary choices. Neither factorial combination formulas nor binomial-sum nodes are required.
